title: Preference-Based Optimisation for Integrated Design and Group Decision-Making
summary: Conventional multi-objective optimisation approaches (e.g., MOO-CP or MIP) fail in group decision-making by aggregating heterogeneous objectives without a valid preference foundation, producing Pareto sets instead of a unique actionable decision. As only humans define objectives, preferences constitute the legitimate basis for decision-making.
